history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration further strengthen its monitoring of the process of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework cycle and identify the causes of backlogs in the above-mentioned countries’ resident coordinator offices, together with the parties involved, to facilitate the completion of the key steps in the Cooperation Framework.
history.administration_response: At its September 2021 meeting, the United Nations Sustainable Development Group discussed the challenges faced by United Nations country teams in meeting the ambition of the timeline for the design of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework guidance. The key issue identified is that many country teams start the design process more than 12 months ahead of implementation so as to enable the submission of agency-specific programme documents, in particular those of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), to their governing boards (generally submitted in June for a September board, i.e. 7 months before implementation commences). The United Nations Sustainable Development Group Principals agreed to re-examine the design timelines for Cooperation Frameworks and agree on a standard target duration prior to implementation as a way forward. An inter-agency technical group, led by the Development Coordination Office, will initiate discussions in April 2022 to analyse current trends and provide recommendations to the Group on design timelines. In parallel, United Nations system entities agreed to re-examine their own specific country programme development processes, which are impacting the timeline for Cooperation Framework design.
history.board_assessment: Given that the efforts made by the Development Coordination Office, and the design timelines for Cooperation Frameworks will be re-examined, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration further strengthen its monitoring of the process of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework cycle and identify the causes of backlogs in the above- mentioned countries’ resident coordinator offices, together with parties involved, to facilitate the completion of the key steps in the Cooperation Framework.
history.administration_response: The United Nations Sustainable Development Group principals meeting in October 2022 discussed the trend analysis on United Nations entity derivation from United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks, which touched upon the overall timelines for design. These trends – consistent with the 2021 audit observations – showed that the time taken to design Cooperation Frameworks remains longer than that outlined in the guidelines. The timelines are guidelines, not rules, and will need to be tailored to the country context. That said, the Development Coordination Office continues to monitor and identify systemic solutions to shorten the design timeline. An independent, system-wide evaluation on good practices and opportunities for improvement of country programme derivation from and alignment with Cooperation Frameworks and United Nations country team configurations across all United Nations Sustainable Development Group entities (undertaken by the soon-to-be established United Nations Sustainable Development Group System-wide Evaluation Office) will serve to inform any policy revisions and/or practice adjustments. While solutions are being identified, the Development Coordination Office requests that the Board close this recommendation, as process monitoring and the identification of backlogs has been completed. Translating this work into shorter time frames will require system-wide solutions that are beyond the immediate control of the Development Coordination Office.
history.board_assessment: Given that the systematic backlogs of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework cycle have not yet been addressed, and further system-wide evaluation on the Cooperation Framework cycle is needed, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration further strengthen its monitoring of the process of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework cycle and identify the causes of backlogs in the above- mentioned countries’ resident coordinator offices, together with the parties involved, to facilitate the completion of the key steps in the Cooperation Framework.
history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office continues to monitor preparation timelines for cooperation frameworks through its standardized weekly and monthly engagements with regional and country offices. During the last quarter of 2023, the Development Coordination Office initiated the process of light review of the existing United Nations Sustainable Development Group Cooperation Framework guidance. The review has made adjustments to the road map chapter which now clarifies that the timelines of the overall process and each milestone are indicative and estimated at 9−12 months. The outcome has been a lightened and streamlined process that has accelerated the Cooperation Framework preparation process. Therefore, the Development Coordination Office suggests that the Board close this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given the completion of the light review and the adjustments to the guidance road map for the United Nations Sustainable Development Group Cooperation Framework, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
